    Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio

    risk_calc_location_quotient.Rd

    Calculates a location quotient as the local rate divided by the reference rate. This follows the general approach used by Boscoe and Pradhan (2015), who mapped the most distinctive cause of death by comparing state-specific age-adjusted mortality rates with national age-adjusted mortality rates.

    Usage

    risk_calc_location_quotient(
  data,
  observed_col = "event_count",
  denominator_col,
  reference_rate = NULL,
  lq_col = "location_quotient",
  local_rate_col = "local_rate",
  min_count = 0
)

    Arguments

    data

    A data frame or sf object.

    observed_col

    Column containing observed counts.

    denominator_col

    Column containing population, exposure, or denominator.

    reference_rate

    Optional fixed reference rate. If NULL, the reference rate is calculated from all rows.

    lq_col

    Name of output location quotient column.

    local_rate_col

    Name of local rate output column.

    min_count

    Minimum observed count required before calculating LQ.

    Value

    Input data with local rate and location quotient columns.

    References

    Boscoe FP, Pradhan E. The Most Distinctive Causes of Death by State, 2001–2010. Preventing Chronic Disease. 2015;12:E75. doi:10.5888/pcd12.140395.

    Examples

    data <- data.frame(
  event_count = c(5, 10, 20),
  population = c(1000, 2000, 3000)
)

risk_calc_location_quotient(
  data = data,
  observed_col = "event_count",
  denominator_col = "population"
)
#>   event_count population  local_rate location_quotient
#> 1           5       1000 0.005000000         0.8571429
#> 2          10       2000 0.005000000         0.8571429
#> 3          20       3000 0.006666667         1.1428571
